inputs.dem_height_datum: NAVD88 orthometric metres, as USGS states for 3DEP seamless; GEOID18 (world.terrain.geoid18) takes them to the NAD83(2011) ellipsoid
inputs.geoid_height_datum: metres from the NAD83(2011) ellipsoid up to the NAVD88 surface: an ellipsoid height is h = H + N, H a NAVD88 height and N this value

inputs.ground_height_datum: NAVD88 orthometric metres, as USGS states for every 3DEP DEM (the GeoTIFF's CRS has no vertical part); GEOID18 (world.terrain.geoid18) takes them to the NAD83(2011) ellipsoid
inputs.surface_height_datum: NAVD88 orthometric metres, as the 3DEP 1 m DEM's: the EPT's srs states no vertical datum, so it was measured -- 823,384 class-2 returns over cs-downtown sit 0.000 m (median, IQR 0.028 m) from the DEM's cells (2026-11-01). GEOID18 (world.terrain.geoid18) takes them to the NAD83(2011) ellipsoid

surface.height_datum: NAD83(2011) ellipsoid metres: h = H + N, H the highest of the 1 m lidar surface and every 1 m DEM file (NAVD88) in the cell holding the point and N GEOID18's, bilinear; used as WGS84 ellipsoid metres, about 1 m off in CONUS, not corrected

terrain.height_datum: NAD83(2011) ellipsoid metres: h = H + N, H the 3DEP DEM's NAVD88 height and N GEOID18's, each sampled bilinearly; used as WGS84 ellipsoid metres, about 1 m off in CONUS, not corrected

assumptions: Each leg is the WGS84 geodesic between its waypoints (Vincenty inverse and direct); height above the ellipsoid changes linearly along it.

A leg flies at constant ground speed and vertical rate, ending both together; its duration is the longer of the leg at cruise speed and the height change at the climb or descent rate. Turns and speed changes are instantaneous.
No wind acts on any leg.
No terrain avoidance: terrain is read at every row and a row below it refuses the run; between rows it is not checked.

Ground speed and course are along the ellipsoid; the state velocity is them and the vertical rate in the local east-north-up frame, so it omits the h/R growth of horizontal rate at height (about 0.03 % at 2 km).
Earth-fixed to ECI by a GMST rotation about z only (wgs84-geodetic-to-eci-gmst/1); no precession, nutation or polar motion.
The drone profile's values are the scenario's own declaration, illustrative, not a measured airframe.
The profile's lost-link block is declared but no failsafe is flown by this model: every row is mode 0 (mission).
WGS84 longitude and latitude are read as NAD83 with no horizontal transform (about 1 m in CONUS); stated, not corrected.
h = H + N is NAD83(2011) ellipsoid metres, used as WGS84 ellipsoid metres (about 1 m in CONUS); stated, not corrected.

One synthetic emitter fixed at a WGS84 geodetic site (height above the ellipsoid, 0-9000 m), above the obstacle surface in its cell; terrain, buildings and trees enter only as that surface's knife edges.
The WGS84 ellipsoid is opaque; paths that touch it are blocked. Visibility also requires geodetic elevation at or above the declared horizon mask.
The horizon mask is caller policy for site obstruction, not a computed terrain or antenna horizon.
FSPL = 20 log10(4 pi r f / c); received power = EIRP times receiver gain divided by attenuation and system loss.
EIRP and receiver gain are fixed in the path direction; no antenna pattern, attitude or polarization calculation.
No atmosphere, troposphere, ionosphere, refraction, rain, multipath, light-time or Doppler; diffraction only over the obstacle surface's knife edges.
All modeled interference is assumed in the declared common band; no spectral-overlap or waveform calculation.
min_range_m is an explicit caller validity policy; antenna far-field conditions are assumed, not verified.

The desired signal S is propagated from GCS gcs-1, at the WGS84 site and EIRP declared in configuration.signal.gcs (height above the ellipsoid, 0-9000 m), by the same free-space model, frequency, receiver gain and system loss as the interference; it is not prescribed. Noise remains a prescribed receiver-plane input.
S is 0 when the GCS path touches the opaque ellipsoid. No horizon mask applies to the GCS path, and min_range_m bounds it as it bounds the emitter's path.

Obstacle heights are the highest of the class-1 lidar return and every 1 m DEM file holding a value in the 1 m cell holding each path point; every return is an opaque edge (buildings and trees alike).
WGS84 longitude and latitude are read as NAD83 and projected to NAD83 / UTM with no datum transform (about 1 m, one cell, in CONUS); stated, not corrected.

Obstruction (dataforge.p526-knife-edge-deygout/1): each ground path is the straight chord from the site's antenna to the receiver, sampled every 1 m from 1 m to 1 m short of its end; each sample's obstacle top is the surface height in its cell, and its clearance is its signed distance from the chord.

Edge loss is ITU-R P.526-15's single knife edge, J(nu) for nu > -0.78; edges combine by Deygout's construction limited to three (the main edge, then one per side), summed with no empirical correction.
A path whose largest nu is at most -0.78 is clear and keeps its free-space power exactly. No refraction, ground reflection or vegetation loss; every obstacle is an opaque edge.
The scenario time grid provides timing, half-open at its last epoch; it carries no radiated power or receiver calibration.
semantic_metadata.attribution: Foundation C-UAS simulation (intelpayloads/dataforge-plugin-foundation), completed-run contract dataforge.completed-simulation-run/1 with a dataforge.uas-track/1 artifact (GEN-355). SIMULATED, not observed: a deterministic kinematic flight with an in-kernel lost-link failsafe; the C2 powers are free space over an opaque ellipsoid, and on a run whose terrain pins a lidar surface (GEN-404) the GCS path also loses its ITU-R P.526 knife-edge diffraction over it: c2_obstruction_loss_db in dB, c2_obstructed, the edge count, and the main edge's lon/lat, top and ground under it (m above the ellipsoid), c2_edge_roofed (a building or tree) and nu; null on a free-space run. mode_code, c2_state_code and c2_reason_code legends are the header's mode_codes, c2_state_codes and c2_reason_codes. A null is unknown, never a fabricated outage
semantic_metadata.height_datum: height_m is Foundation's height above the WGS84 ellipsoid from the flight kernel's geodetic state; terrain_height_m and height_agl_m use the region's NAVD88 DEM taken to NAD83(2011) ellipsoid metres by GEOID18, treated as WGS84 (about 1 m apart in CONUS, not corrected)

c2_edge_nu.meaning: the main edge's diffraction parameter ν (ITU-R P.526); null when clear

c2_sinr_db.meaning: 10·log10(S / (N + I)); null when I is unknown (state unknown) or when S is 0 (reason no_desired_signal)

course_deg.meaning: direction of horizontal motion, clockwise from true north, [0, 360); null when ground_speed_mps is 0

c2_margin_db.meaning: c2_sinr_db − c2_unavailable_below_sinr_db; below 0 the link is unavailable; null when c2_sinr_db is

height_agl_m.meaning: height_m − terrain_height_m, computed from the flown height, never the planned clearance

c2_obstructed.meaning: the GCS path is diffracted: some edge has ν > −0.78; null when occulted

c2_state_code.meaning: the C2 receiver's state; c2_state_codes (the RF state legend)

c2_edge_roofed.meaning: the lidar surface set the main edge's top, so a building or tree; false when it is bare earth; null when clear

c2_reason_code.meaning: why; c2_reason_codes (the RF reason legend, which includes code 10)

c2_edge_lat_deg.meaning: latitude of the GCS path's main edge; null when clear

c2_edge_lon_deg.meaning: longitude of the GCS path's main edge (its largest ν); null when clear

c2_edge_height_m.meaning: height of the main edge's obstacle top above the WGS84 ellipsoid; null when clear

c2_noise_power_w.meaning: N, the receiver's declared noise power

ground_speed_mps.meaning: horizontal speed of the state at this epoch

terrain_height_m.meaning: the region's terrain under the drone, as ellipsoid metres (see "Heights")

c2_signal_power_w.meaning: S, the GCS uplink power at the C2 receiver; 0 when the GCS path does not reach the drone

vertical_speed_mps.meaning: rate of change of height_m, positive up

lost_link_elapsed_s.meaning: the lost-link timer: time since the C2 link was last available, 0 while it is available; see "Lost link". It is null only at an unknown epoch after the failsafe has latched.

lost_link_timeout_s.meaning: the profile's timeout, constant per drone

c2_obstruction_edges.meaning: number of edges in c2_obstruction_loss_db, 0 to 3

c2_nominal_min_sinr_db.meaning: the C2 receiver response's nominal threshold, constant per drone

c2_obstruction_loss_db.meaning: knife-edge diffraction loss on the GCS path over the obstacle surface, up to three Deygout edges; 0 when clear; null when the ellipsoid occults it

c2_edge_ground_height_m.meaning: the bare earth under the main edge (its 1 m DEM cell plus GEOID18) above the WGS84 ellipsoid; null when clear or when no DEM file holds the cell

c2_interference_power_w.meaning: I, the total in-band interference at the C2 receiver; null when unknown

c2_unavailable_below_sinr_db.meaning: the C2 receiver response's unavailable threshold, constant per drone

semantic_metadata.valid_time_basis: the row's epoch on the run's UTC time grid, an ISO-8601 instant with its offset
